## How to read the tables

- The tables are made by code from the bar's records (one JSON record per set, body, seed block, row and condition); each line cites its record, with paths relative to the study directory (hardware/trex_form_study).  Beside the records they read the run directory's `budget.json`, `COST.md`, `dev_episodes.json` (the ledger, the rates, the build's check episodes), each set's `set.json`, `refs.json`, `transitions.json` under the study directory (its latest freeze and the conditions it holds no reference for), the reference check that freeze cites (`refcheck.json`) and today's source hashes of the panels and of the bar.  `bar_tables.json` holds under `checks.inputs` the sha256 of every file read and of this module.
- Readings stand in the plan's order and are never pooled: reading 1 (with the look) is "not defined for this set" (the records say: not defined: the set has no look bands); reading 2 is every limit; reading 3 is every limit but for A1 (the sustained-drive term read on the leg drives only).
- Counts, bounds and passes are the records' own.  A bound is the one-sided 95 % Clopper-Pearson lower bound of the share of the block's 20 episodes.
- A measured value never stands in a column that holds a target or a limit: a column headed "measured" holds measurements, a column headed "Limit" or "as defined" holds none.  A measured median is printed as "median (n)" and a largest value over a record's episodes as "largest (n)": n is the number of episodes that give the quantity, "- (0)" where none does (every episode fell before the judged span); a limit that the tables read from the episodes then reads "not in the record (no episode holds it)".
- A line that prints a controller's verdict on a walk or a turn whose reference's own toe reading is under the kinematic check's limit carries that reading and the limit in its labels (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md C3); the verdict word is the runner's and is not changed for it.
- Wherever the toe term of a walk or a turn is printed (the measured values, the failed terms), the reference's own reading of that term stands beside it in a column of its own kind, "reference: played kinematically, no physics" (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md C3): the reference this condition plays, read by the runner's kinematic check (`refcheck.json`, cited by the set's latest freeze and read only when its sha256 is the cited one).  It is neither a measurement of the robot nor a limit; where the check could not be read, or the record was made on another freeze than the one whose check was read, the cell says so and holds no number.
- Numbers: counts as integers; m with 3 decimals, m/s with 3 decimals, s with 2 decimals, deg with 1 decimal, mm with 2 decimals, ratio with 3 decimals, bound with 3 decimals, m/s^2 with 2 decimals, strides with 2 decimals, N with 1 decimal, core-h with 3 decimals, rad/s with 4 decimals; every other number with %g.
- Every line of set F25F9cl carries the label "margin set after results on seeds 3042-3061": its duty and lift were set after the pull request's results on those seeds (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A3).
- A line of a set whose lead-in is not `start` carries the label "lead-in `<name>`" (the exception of STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A8 for a set without a frozen `nominal` walk, changed after a result): the lead-in is read from the record's own `lead_in` ("as the record says"), and for a cell with no record from the set's `set.json` ("as the set's `set.json` says"); it is never assumed.
- A cell with no record reads "cut by the pre-registered order" where `budget.json` lists its record under a cut unit, or where a unit of its task was cut and the cell, one of the registered order's, is in no started unit.  Else it reads "not run" with its reason, never the bare words: "not run yet" for a cell of the registered order whose unit has not started, or has started and has written no record for it (the unit is named); "not run: in no unit of the registered order of this round (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6)" for a cell the order does not hold (a ladder rung at a delay the order does not read, a set or a body outside the round); and, where the set itself holds no reference for the condition, that reason with the set's own numbers.  A count per verdict word counts all of these under "not run".
- A record whose counts, bounds or passes do not recompute from its own episodes (`bar.counts`; listed under Checks) gives no pass word, no verdict word and no replication word: its cells read "not judged here: the record's counts do not recompute from its episodes", and its counts are printed as the record holds them, flagged.
- A record made later at the path of a finished one is labelled "re-run after a result" with its reason, and the registered record's counts and verdict stand beside it (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md rule R2).
- Rules amended after a result, with the plan's own labels (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md):

- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.

- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.

- The rungs in ascending order: the nominal walk, then 0.3 to 0.5 m/s; the 0.40 m/s rung's records are table 1's.  "none" says no rung passes under both rows, whether its records fail, are not run or are cut: each rung's own cell says which.  A rung named here is the highest among the rungs that have a verdict at that delay.  Where a rung above it has none (not run, cut or incomplete) the cell says "no verdict above it for" and names those rungs, or "the only rung with a verdict at this delay (each other rung's own cell says why it has none)" where no other rung has one: the named rung is then no ceiling of the speed.
- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.

## 3. The rest of the bar (task 4): turns, nudges and the stop

- The 14 gated conditions (the quick turn each way, a nudge from each of four sides, the two-touchdown stop, on both grips) and the reported ladders (turn rates, nudges at 0.375 and 0.5 x the push bound, Stage 1's one-step stop).  Every item starts with the walk's lead-in and takes the walk's seed slot: a fall before the command is a fall of the lead-in and shows in every item of that seed.
- A turn without a reference is "not run" with its reason and the reference's own numbers: that is no result of the robot.  It goes to the owner and has no fallback (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A11).
- `stop/one_step` plays Stage 1's non-causal stop and is read from Stage 1's command; its lines say so.

- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.

## 4. The bar at a glance: the 16 gated conditions at 10 ms

- Per set and body, the verdict of the controller R2 (rows R2/42@10ms and R2/43@10ms) on each gated condition, in each reading.  A cell reads "not run" with its reason: the set holds no reference for the condition, the condition is in no unit of this round's registered order, or its unit has not started yet (or has started and has not written the record); none of these is a pass, and none is a result of the robot.
- A line of a walk or a turn whose reference's own toe reading is under the kinematic check's limit carries that reading in its labels (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md C3: such a condition is expected to fail the toe term for a reason that is in the reference; the verdict words are the runner's and are not changed for it).

- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.
- Rules amended after a result, with the plan's own labels (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md):
  - A7 [changed 15 Nov after a result: the review's scratch builds of V0's stop and quick turn (prescribed motion); before any set was frozen and before any closed-loop episode on a Stage 2 set] The two causal limits each read their own frames. (the limits themselves were changed by the next entry)
  - A7 [changed 15 Nov after a result, by the owner's decision (`DECISION_LOG.md` P34): the first builds of the three sets, `stage2/design/checkpoint/SETS_FIRST_BUILD.md`; prescribed motion, before any set was frozen and before any closed-loop episode on a Stage 2 set] The ZMP readings of a causal move have one limit, Stage 1's 4.0 mm: the warm-up frames against the walk's (`join_command`; it was 2.0 mm), the consistency error over the first stride after the command (it was 2.5 mm), and the ZMP error after that stride (4.0 mm, unchanged).
  - A8 [changed 15 Nov after a result, by the owner's decision (`DECISION_LOG.md` P34): the first builds of the three sets, `stage2/design/checkpoint/SETS_FIRST_BUILD.md`; prescribed motion, before any set was frozen and before any closed-loop episode on a Stage 2 set] A set whose `nominal` walk is not frozen but whose `v0.4` walk is starts from standing straight into its 0.40 m/s walk (`start_v0.4`), and its lead-in is that start followed by the 0.40 m/s walk; `set.json` and every record of the set say so (`lead_in: "start_v0.4"`).
  - A11 [changed 15 Nov after a result: the set screen's review read the design's scratch prototypes of V0's quick turn at `f` 0.8 and found the inside leg's hip roll 0.086 rad from its limit, under A12's 0.10 rad, which by the third outcome above would have left the turn without a reference; prescribed motion; before any set was frozen and before any closed-loop episode on a Stage 2 set] The stride rule also reads A12's joint range (the plan's sentence goes on; this amendment was withdrawn as written by the next entry)

- Verdict words (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H2): at the judged delay (10 ms) `shown` if both R2 rows pass and `provisional` if one does, in reading 3 with `but for A1`; at another delay the cell reads `passes at <ms> ms` and is no verdict.  Where neither row passes at the judged delay the cell reads "neither row passes: " and the runner's failing word (Stage 1's: `controller-limited`, `body-limited`, or `not attributed` while the records' falls have not been attributed): that is a fail, never a pass.  At another delay a cell of reading 3 in which neither row passes reads "does not pass at <ms> ms, also with A1 set aside" (the runner's word for it ends "but for A1", the name of the reading, and is no pass with A1 set aside).  An R0 row gives no verdict and is not replicated.  A candidate's `shown` or `provisional` stands with the replication word of each row's record that passed.  The registered order (STAGE2_75_PLAN.md H6) holds no replication of task 3's tier 9 (the speed ladder at 4 and 6 ms) and none of task 4's tier 6 (the reported ladders at 10 ms): beside a pass of the candidate there stands "replication cut by the pre-registered order (the order holds no replication unit for it)", whatever the ledger shows.

## The runner's rules these tables rest on

- `readings`: every episode is read three ways, in the plan's order and never pooled: (1) shown with the look: not defined for a set without look bands (the block is null with that reason); (2) every limit (success); (3) every limit but for A1 (success_but_A1): the same terms with the sustained-drive term read on the leg drives only (plant.leg_drives: every drive but the neck's and the tail's).  The drives' RMS is taken over the judged window for the walk and the turn and over the whole episode for nudges and the stop; both spans' per-drive ratios are recorded.  A turn frozen with a1_over runs and records both readings, but reading 2 gives it no verdict (not read: a1_over, which is not a pass)
- `pass_`: a record passes a reading if all 20 episodes of its block survive and at least 17 succeed in that reading; a record of fewer episodes, of other seeds or with an episode that failed to run is not judged.  The judged delay is 10 ms; at another delay a record 'passes at <ms> ms' and gives no verdict.  R0 rows, Stage 1's reading, the replication block alone and a control give no verdict
- `replication`: of the 75 cm round's sets only F25F9cl (the candidate) is replicated: every seeds3042 record of it under a row with a verdict that passes in reading 2 or in reading 3 is run again on seeds5042 with the same row; the controls are not run on seeds5042; the new record names the record and the reading that triggered it (replication_of); the blocks are never pooled; a pass of an R0 row is not replicated.  Beside a shown or provisional verdict stands, for each row's record that passed, 'replicated' (the second block's record passes in that reading), 'not replicated' or 'replication cut by the pre-registered order'
- `seeds`: blocks: seeds3042 (3042-3061, the headline) and seeds5042 (5042-5061, replication); an episode's start, sensor-noise and push seeds are tune.derived_seed(seed, 0, purpose) (panels.EPISODE_RULE with slot 0 for every item)
- `budget`: a task's budget is the sum of its episodes' wall seconds (attribution's lifted episodes and re-runs included) in budget.json.  It is spent unit by unit (one run command; one record's attribution): a unit starts only if the task's spent core-hours plus the unit's estimate (its planned simulated seconds x the committed rates) fit; a started unit finishes; the first unit that does not fit is cut with every unit after it
- `no_overwrite`: a finished record ('done' or 'not run') whose key differs is never replaced silently: the run stops with the differing key fields, and so it does for a record file that cannot be read; --supersede moves the old record to <record>.superseded/<first 12 hex of its key's sha256>.json and the new record states its reason (supersedes.reason): it is a re-run after a result.  The label is written beside the kept record (<12 hex>.reason.json) before the record is moved, and every later record at that path carries it, so a killed re-run keeps it; supersedes.registered names the first record made at the path, supersedes.replaces the one just moved; the moved record's traces go to eval/traces.superseded/<12 hex>/
